standard.title: Analyse and summarise ideas
standard.description: Use comprehension strategies such as visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising, monitoring, questioning and inferring to analyse and summarise information and ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: Students use comprehension strategies including visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising, monitoring and questioning to build literal and inferred meaning (AC9E6LY05). They have not yet used these strategies to explicitly analyse and summarise — moving from building meaning to synthesising and distilling it.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use comprehension strategies including inferring to analyse and summarise information and ideas.

nodes.label: Inferring beyond the literal
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use inferencing to construct meaning beyond the literal content of a text
nodes.minimum_width: In a given text, identify a point where the meaning is implied rather than stated and explain what inference a reader needs to make — what information is assumed, and how does the reader fill the gap?
nodes.typical_width: Apply inferencing across a range of text types — reading between the lines in narrative, inferring unstated causes in explanation, inferring implied attitudes in persuasive texts — and explain the inferential reasoning in each case
wider: Analyse visual features including choice of image, colour, composition and font in covers of different editions of books — what inferences about tone, genre and audience does each cover invite?
Compare how formal and informal speeches imply different things about the speaker's attitude to the audience — what is inferred from formality level that is never stated?

response_modes.reason: Inferencing is an implicit mental operation students perform naturally but cannot always articulate. Making the reasoning explicit — what is stated, what is not stated, what background knowledge enables the gap to be filled — is the scaffold that transforms an unconscious reading behaviour into an analysable comprehension strategy.

success_criteria: Identifies a point in a text where meaning is implied rather than stated
Explains the inferential reasoning — what is assumed and how the gap is filled

nodes.label: Summarising key ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can determine and summarise the key ideas of paragraphs and extended texts
nodes.minimum_width: Determine the key idea of a given paragraph and write a one-sentence summary; explain what was included and what was omitted and why
nodes.typical_width: Summarise the key ideas of an extended text, making decisions about what to include and what to omit; explain how the summary captures the essential meaning without reproducing the text's full detail
wider: Determine and summarise the key ideas of paragraphs and chapters in an extended text — practise multi-level summarising (paragraph → section → whole text)
Compare the presentation of ideas in formal and informal speeches and determine the key ideas in each — discuss why the same ideas may be summarised differently depending on context

response_modes.reason: Summarising is a high-frequency skill that degrades to copying or listing without sustained practice. The precision required — distinguishing key ideas from supporting detail, and capturing essential meaning in fewer words — develops through repeated application across varied text types and lengths.

success_criteria: Identifies the key idea of a given paragraph
Writes a summary that captures essential meaning without reproducing the full text
